From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@freshline.com>

Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow up after demo — econ details + trial ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for walking us through the Redwood demo today — the routing and KV cache bits were impressive and should help our latency goals. Per our internal discussion here are the econ details we need to lock down to make a pilot decision:

- Pilot window: 30 days starting as soon as we have an extension/credits in place
- Expected burn (pilot): ~3–6M tokens total in the 30-day window (mix of short prompts ~120 tokens and longer runs ~1,200 tokens; avg ~340 tokens/request)
- Target budget range for pilot: $10k–$25k (we can go to the high end if unit economics justify)
- Target unit price we’d like to see: ~$1,500–$2,000 per 1M tokens (we understand this may vary by throughput/commitment)

Two asks from us: 1) Could you confirm an indicative price for the pilot volumes above? 2) Are you able to approve a short-term credit to cover initial burn while we validate integration?

We’re aiming to decide by early next week. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Moreno
Head of Product
Freshline Foods

Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow up after demo — econ details + trial ask

Alicia — thanks for the clear summary and numbers, this is super helpful. Quick recap and what we can offer:

- Pilot sizing: 3–6M tokens over 30 days aligns with a small scoped integration. If average request is ~340 tokens, that maps to ~9k–18k requests total.
- Indicative pricing (hosted API, no long-term commit):
  • Small pilot band (<=10M/mo): $2,200 per 1M tokens
  • Mid band (>=10M/mo): $1,700 per 1M tokens (volume-based)

Given your target of $1.5k–$2k per 1M, I can propose a one-time pilot microgrant to bridge the initial validation costs. Suggested offer: $5,000 credit applied to the pilot (30-day validity), plus a short extension of the trial. Conditions we’d ask for: basic guardrails (rate caps + per-request token cap) and a short onboarding checklist so we can measure quality/latency.

To move forward I need two things from your side: 1) confirm you’ll enable the guardrails (I’ve attached a short template), and 2) who on your side will be the technical owner for integration (name + email). If you confirm, I’ll loop in our sales ops for a formal microgrant approval and get the credits provisioned.

Shall we aim to have this finalized by Tue morning PST? I’m happy to get on a 15-min call if needed.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
